value: TWO assumptions carried into the build rather than left standing. (1) That the heavy probes' answers are pure functions of the corpus on disk - if one legitimately depends on a clock, a live host or a database row, no fingerprint can be right for it. Unverified per probe, and it is the FIRST thing the build establishes: getting it wrong produces a fast beat answering with stale truth, which is worse than a slow one. (2) That the fingerprint is cheap - a stat sweep over ~331 files is assumed cheap and unmeasured, and if it costs a meaningful slice of a second the approach changes shape.

Whether these questions belong on a heartbeat AT ALL. A corpus-wide import census is a build-time question and the tester already owns that shape. Moving work is not making it cheap, and which probes belong on a beat is a design conversation - not a decision to smuggle into a performance node. FOR AKIEN.
